title: State: services with signals, and an overview of NgRx

videos.script:
Since lesson eleven, the planner has kept its state in a service of signals. This lesson names that pattern and uses it again. Then it looks at the library most large Angular applications use instead.

{{pattern}} Data flows one way. An event calls a method, and the method replaces the state. Whatever depends on the state follows.

{{preferences}} A second store holds a preference: hide the sessions that are done. It survives moving between pages. A reload loses it.

{{persisting}} So an effect writes it to local storage. That is the outside world an effect is for, and now the preference outlives the visit.

{{ngrx}} Then N g R x Store, installed for a bench. Actions, a reducer and selectors: the same idea, with every part made explicit.

{{which}} And a table for choosing. A library changes how the answer is written down, not what the answer is.
